dish.title: Bhutanese Ema Datshi: Green Chiles in Farmer's Cheese Sauce with Red Rice
dish.description: Halved Anaheim chiles and jalapenos, stems left on, simmered with onion, tomatoes, garlic, and butter, then melted into a loose, tangy sauce of farmer's cheese and feta, served over nutty Bhutanese red rice.

recipe_version.title: Bhutanese Ema Datshi: Green Chiles in Farmer's Cheese Sauce with Red Rice
recipe_version.description: Halved Anaheim chiles and jalapenos, stems left on, simmered with onion, tomatoes, garlic, and butter, then melted into a loose, tangy sauce of farmer's cheese and feta, served over nutty Bhutanese red rice.

ingredients.name: farmer's cheese
ingredients.display_name: farmer's cheese whose label lists cultured milk and salt (acid-set, no animal rennet) or microbial enzymes

ingredients.name: feta
ingredients.display_name: feta made with microbial or vegetable rennet

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Rinse the rice until the rinse runs clear. Halve the Anaheims and jalapenos lengthwise, leaving the stems on. Slice the onion and garlic, chop the tomatoes, and crumble both cheeses.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: Combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 tsp salt in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, then cover, turn to low, and cook 20 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat to rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the ema datshi
steps.body: While the rice cooks (overlap stated): put the chiles, onion, 1 1/2 cups water, butter, and 1/2 tsp salt in the 3-quart saucepan, cover, and simmer over medium until the chile halves soften, about 12 minutes. Add the tomatoes and garlic and simmer uncovered 4 minutes. Lower the heat, add both cheeses, and stir gently until melted into a loose sauce, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Fluff the rice and serve the ema datshi spooned beside it.

scaling_notes.2: Half of everything in a 2-quart saucepan for the chiles and a 1-quart saucepan for 3/4 cup rice.

coverage_contribution: Bhutan and the Himalaya have only a Nepali potato-bamboo curry in the catalog, and no chile-and-cheese stew exists. A vegetarian dinner with a new main vegetable (green chiles as the bulk).
near_duplicate_review: Compared with chiles-rellenos-ranchero: chile strips melted into a cheese sauce over rice, not whole stuffed battered chiles. Compared with saag-paneer: green chiles in a loose melted farmer's cheese sauce, not spinach with cubes of paneer. Compared with mexican-rajas-con-crema-tacos: no crema and no tortillas; the cheese is the sauce and the rice is red rice.
not_duplicate_of: Not queso fundido and not a chile con queso dip.
